title.narrative: Integrated multisectoral Emergency Response to Drought Affected Communities in Meket Woreda, North Wollo Zone of Amhara Region, Ethiopia

description.narrative: ltpgtThe action addresses the immediate humanitarian needs of 49,634 droughts (and conflict) affected people in Meket Woreda The project is designed and will be implemented by ZOA (lead and sector specialist for Agriculture and WASH Interventions), and local NGO (Action for Social Development and Environmental Protection Organization [ASDEPO] sub-applicant and sector specialist for Nutrition and Health) to address multisectoral Nutrition, Health, Agriculture and WASH needs of drought and conflict-affected community in Meket. The action follows a holistic and integrated approach that leverages the expertise, resources, and local experience of the partners and grassroots community and government structures. During the project design and the next phases of the project cycle management, ZOA and ASDEPO follow an approach of joint planning, implementation, and monitoring of humanitarian interventions that target the same people, at the same time, in the same place, based on a common objective and a shared analysis of needs and priorities. ltbrgtThe project’s Agricultural intervention focuses on increasing targeted beneficiaries' food and nutrition security by creating access to agricultural inputs: provision of improved drought-resistant, nutrition-dense dense and agroecologically harmonized crop seeds, and fertilizers. The project’s agriculture intervention also focuses on the protection of productive livestock assets by providing animal health treatment and vaccination, promoting the production of animal feed through the provision of forage seed, creating access to basic services, and contributing to the protection of productive assets through the provision of multipurpose cash. The project’s Nutrition services include logistical support to smoothen commodity pipelines, and technical assistance to support health facilities (HFs), and frontline health workers in the prevention and treatment of Acute Malnutrition (AM), benefiting 17,200 individuals. The project’s WASH activities will seek to improve access to safe and clean water, sanitation facilities hygiene promotion, and WASH NFI supplies, reaching 14,880. Under Health, the project will assist vaccination campaigns, establish and support Mobile Health and Nutrition Teams, and health facilities (HFs) improve access to quality Reproductive, Maternal, Newborn, and Child Health (RMNCH) services, and strengthen referral linkages. All proposed sectoral interventions are identified based on the rapid need assessment findings conducted in April 2024, and implementation of the action will be guided by the national/sub-national sectoral cluster standards. The project will coordinate with other implementers in Meket woreda to avoid duplication of effort and resources. Accordingly, a head of the project launching, consultative meeting will be held with similar actors in the intervention areas including GOAL Ethiopia to discuss and define coordination mechanisms.lt/pgt
